name: Frame by Frame
brand: NIGHT WINDOW / A film in 72 frames
thesis: A film’s timeline can become the publication’s reading surface.

brief:
**Idea.** A film’s timeline can become the publication’s reading surface.

**Composition.** A dark cinema frame, perforated film edges and a huge translucent frame number occupy the opening. The original moving image is immediately present; jog controls and an unbroken contact strip sit on the film stock, without an explanatory hero.

**Navigation and complete example.** Scrub an original 72-frame vector vignette, select one of six annotated moments, compare the storyboard with the finished scene and read its production notes.

**Responsive and inclusive behaviour.** The phone screen is a tall contained film frame, followed directly by jog controls and a horizontal chapter strip. Playback is opt-in and all annotations are reachable while paused. Native buttons, visible focus, a direct return path and reduced-motion support preserve access to the same content.

**Adaptation.** Attach information to meaningful temporal moments. Use a finite timeline and make motion pausable; do not require playback to access annotations. Retain the relationship between navigation and content. Do not reduce the reference to a generic hero followed by interchangeable cards.

**Research.** [Aaron Koblin — The Wilderness Downtown](https://www.aaronkoblin.com/project/the-wilderness-downtown/). These are conceptual precedents, not copied artwork, source code, branding or text. All diagrams and sample writing in this specimen are original, fictional material.
scope: Complete visual reference with deterministic local interactions and fictional content; no production backend.
